To download posts from Bluesky and run a network analysis in R, you’ll use the bskyr package to access Bluesky’s API, tidy the data into R-friendly formats, and then apply network analysis libraries like igraph or ggraph. The workflow is: install bskyr → authenticate → pull posts and relationships → clean and structure data → build a graph object → analyze and visualize.

```{r}
#install.packages(c("igraph", "tidygraph", "ggraph", "dplyr"))
#install.packages("bskyr")
```

```{r}
library(bskyr)

bs_user <- bs_get_user()
bs_pass <- bs_get_pass()
bs_Auth <- bs_auth(bs_user, bs_pass, save_auth = TRUE)
```

```{r}
me <- bs_get_profile(actor = bs_user, auth = bs_Auth)
print(me)

```

```{r}
posts <- bs_search_posts("*", tag = 'speirgorm OR SpeirGorm OR Speirgorm', clean = TRUE)

library(stringr)
#posts$hashtags <- str_extract_all(posts$text, "#\\w+")

```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
edges <- posts %>%
  select(author = author$did, reply_to = reply_parent) %>%
  filter(!is.na(reply_to))

nodes <- data.frame(name = unique(c(edges$author, edges$reply_to)))

```

```{r}
library(igraph)
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges, vertices = nodes, directed = TRUE)

```

```{r}
library(ggraph)
ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_node_point(size = 5) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE)

```
